brief.question: Does critical-site sensitivity translate into realizable, graph-specific improvements in low-timestep GCN-to-SNN conversion?
brief.answer: The tested strong-teacher setting separates ideal sensitivity from practical calibration. Message objectives and fixed-budget residual selection do not establish robust structural advantage over matched local and counterfactual controls.
brief.audience: Researchers designing conversion and graph quantization methods who need to distinguish realizability, target mismatch and event-budget effects.
brief.domain_bridge: Graph propagation makes quantization errors directional. Actual next-message perturbations and within-graph operator controls test whether exploiting that direction yields classification gains beyond local reconstruction.

terminology.opportunity budget: upper bound on extra per-channel events, not equal actual energy

section_jobs.Introduction: Present low-prefix graph conversion and sensitivity-realizability question.
section_jobs.Related Work: Separate known calibration, coding, graph quantization and adaptive budgets from this empirical test.
section_jobs.Method: Define teachers, exact event dynamics, loss comparisons, ideal diagnostic and bounded allocation.
section_jobs.Experiments and Results: Organize comparisons by scientific question with their own matched scopes and uncertainty.
section_jobs.Discussion: Explain practical capacity and proxy limitations and hardware implications.
section_jobs.Conclusion: State evidence-scaled empirical answer and remaining method gap.

facts.statement: Frozen four-layer residual GCNs classify MNIST and CIFAR10 superpixel graphs. Four node branches and two readout activations use signed eight-level differential events. Subsequent studies preserve teacher weights.

New comparisons use 512 training calibration graphs and 512 validation graphs from fixed indices. Both official validation and test sets have historical exposure. New methods are selected without loading test; these are exploratory comparisons, not independent external confirmation.

The allocation candidate supplements only the first site at its first tick with signed quantized residual events for ceil(n/4) nodes per graph. Local, feature-only, permuted and actual-message policies share candidates and opportunity budgets. Actual nonzero event counts can differ.

For a fixed folded graph convolution, first-site error E changes the next preactivation by A E W transpose. Residual identity and later nonlinearities remain separate. This linear identity motivates a proxy, not a novel theorem or an exact final-classification model.

Node features and positions are concatenated and embedded to146 channels. Four residual branches apply H_next=H+ReLU(A H W^T+b), with evaluation BN folded into W,b. A[v,u]=1/sqrt(max(outdegree(u),1)*max(indegree(v),1)) on each original u-to-v edge, without extra self-loops. Mean pooling feeds146-to73-to36-to10 linear layers with two hidden ReLUs.

Each baseline site emits zero or a signed amplitude theta*2^(-k), k=0,...,7. At active tick t, pre-event membrane m=v+c+a-b and cumulative Ctilde=C+b. Positive threshold tests use m>=.75*theta*2^(-k); negative emission also requires Ctilde>=theta*2^(-k). After hard selection s: v=m-s, C=Ctilde+s, a=a+c/t, b=b+s/t. Decode sum(s_t/t); raw input and affine biases enter once at the first active tick. These are graded events, not binary spikes.

Teacher weights and channel thresholds stay frozen. Initial membrane is theta*rho with rho initially zero and clipped to[-.5,.5]. Four node146-wide and two readout73/36-wide sites give693 parameters; first-site-only fitting uses146. Screens use the same512 training graphs, batch32 and64 Adam updates at fixed rates .001 and .01. A ReLU membrane surrogate supplies backward derivatives while hard events are unchanged in the forward pass.

All-site local loss averages six site MSEs divided by their batchwise teacher mean-square, denominator floor1e-6. First-site message calibration averages the corresponding local loss and MSE(A E W_next^T)/mean_square(A H_teacher W_next^T). Feature control substitutes identity for A; structural control uses a fixed within-graph conjugation P^-1 A P. Different optimization/storage budgets are separate probes, not pooled matched methods.

Alphabet diagnostic changes only first site to eight nonnegative channel-specific values plus zero with nearest-neighbor midpoint decisions; remaining sites retain their original quantizer. Sixteen weighted Lloyd iterations fit1168 scalars. An additional matched hard-objective probe makes one1168-coordinate sweep from a common local-Lloyd start, considering step fractions1,.5,.25 and retaining the incumbent unless actual hard loss decreases. This exceeds64-step Adam fitting and first146-scalar storage.

The ideal intervention does NOT overwrite a site with teacher activations. It operates on the current incoming converted signal: u_t=u_(t-1)+c_t/t, and emits d_t=t*(ReLU(u_t)-ReLU(u_(t-1))). Thus its weighted prefix is ReLU(u_T); no teacher hidden state is needed. At other idealized sites incoming signals can still differ from teacher signals. The empty intervention matches uncalibrated conversion, and replacing all six sites was empirically verified to reproduce the folded ANN. Individual/group effects are conditional and nonadditive.

The opportunity budget is146*ceil(n/4) scalar extra-event slots PER GRAPH, not146 slots per graph. There are146 slots PER SELECTED NODE. Across512 graphs the MNIST total is1344222 slots (9207 selected nodes) and CIFAR10 is2225186 slots (15241 selected nodes). Actual message-policy nonzero extras are612232 and926039 respectively; different policies can use different actual counts within the same slot budget.

The source-percentile comparator is a GCN adaptation, not a complete reproduction of the author converter. Frozen ANN post-ReLU activations from512 training graphs yield per-channel .999 quantiles, floored at1e-6. The image-source example uses four amplitude levels and threshold scale4 at32 ticks; transplanting it toT1/T2 is a configuration diagnostic. A second fixed preset uses eight levels and scale1 to match the local event alphabet; no validation scale search occurs.

Every alphabet/Lloyd/refined-alphabet probe changes ONLY the first site. Full-message refinement means the complete squared message objective including cross terms, NOT an all-site codebook intervention. Six-site all-local/all-message membrane probes are separate693-offset conditions.

At the first site and first tick, current z is already available. E=s-ReLU(z); candidate correction c is nearest signed quantization of-E using eight geometric amplitudes theta/(4*2^k) plus zero. Select ceil(n/4) nodes per graph, at most146 extra scalar events each. Exact single-node message gain is -2*inner_product(A E W^T,A[:,i](c_i W^T))-norm(A[:,i](c_i W^T))^2. Normalize local and message gains by graphwise teacher energy, average equally and top-k once. Candidate interactions make joint gains nonadditive. Extra events update membrane, cumulative output and decoded output consistently; same T1-fitted base offsets are used at both T1/T2.

Historical full experiments use teacher seeds41,42,43. Official train/validation/test counts are MNIST:55000/5000/10000 and CIFAR10:45000/5000/10000. New method screens use teacher41 and fixed512-graph validation. Report accuracy, own-teacher agreement and logit MSE; distinguish teacher-seed sample SD from exploratory paired graph-sampling intervals. Previously exposed4488 validation graphs outside the initial512 are not an independent external dataset.
